last_assistant_message:
Clean build: `** BUILD SUCCEEDED **`, 0 duplicate warnings, 0 other warnings/errors, `in Sources` count 0 (synchronized group intact). Both features are done and verified.

## Summary

### 1. Fixed the delete-freeze bug
`SavedTermsStore` persisted on every single array mutation (`didSet { save() }`), and `remove(_:)` called `updateSortOrders()`, which reassigned `sortOrder` element-by-element — each write re-encoding the **entire** vocabulary to `UserDefaults` synchronously. Deleting one word from an N-word list did ~N full encodes (O(N²)), freezing the main thread until the OS killed it (SIGTERM). Now each bulk mutation builds a new array and assigns `terms` **once**, so a delete saves a single time. (`remove(at:)`, `remove(chinese:)`, and `move` got the same treatment.)

### 2. Added persistent AI-explanation caching
- **`WordExplanationResult`** and its sub-structs are now `Codable` (transient `id`s excluded from coding keys → no decode warnings).
- **New `WordExplanationCacheStore`** (`Models/WordExplanationCacheStore.swift`): MainActor, `UserDefaults`-backed, LRU-bounded to 400 entries, keyed by normalized word + direction token (`zh>en` etc.) so toggling the interface language never serves a wrong-language explanation. Tolerant decode + single-save-per-mutation (applying the lesson from bug #1).
- **`AIWordExplanationView`** now serves a cached explanation **instantly** on open (no AI round-trip, no token cost), shows a subtle "Saved" badge, and persists every freshly generated explanation. The refresh button forces regeneration and overwrites the cache. It also reconciles correctly if the interface language flips while open.
- **Data Management screen** gained a "Cached AI Explanations" count and a "Clear Cached AI Explanations" action with confirmation.
- **Localization**: 6 new `zh-Hans` strings added additively to `Localizable.xcstrings` (683→689 keys) — no reordering of existing keys, per project convention.

### Housekeeping
A tool had auto-injected explicit source entries into `project.pbxproj` (duplicating files already covered by the synchronized file group, producing 18 "duplicate build file" warnings). I reverted it; the sync group picks up the new file on its own, and the project is back to its zero-warning, `in Sources == 0` convention.

One note for later (didn't touch it — out of scope): the sibling stores `TranslationHistory` and `WorkbookBank` use the same `didSet { save() }` pattern. They don't have a reindex loop so they aren't O(N²), but they're where to look if deleting from history/workbook ever feels slow.

All three issues are fixed and the build is clean (`** BUILD SUCCEEDED **`, zero warnings, `in Sources == 0`, pbxproj clean).

## What I changed

### 1. Kimi Code API key 401 — fixed the misconfiguration
The Kimi **Code** (coding-plan) endpoint is a specialized proxy with rules distinct from the Moonshot Open Platform. I corrected every mismatch:
- **Model** → `kimi-for-coding` (was defaulting to `kimi-k2.7`, which the coding endpoint doesn't accept). This is the single unified model id the coding plan serves; it's now the default and the vision model.
- **API-key link** → `https://www.kimi.com/code/console` (was `platform.kimi.ai` — the Open Platform, whose keys are **not interchangeable** with the coding endpoint). Pointing you at the wrong console was very likely the source of the invalid key.
- **No `/models` listing** → the coding proxy has no `GET /models` route (that's what returned the 401 on auto-refresh). I set Kimi's `modelsPath = nil`, so it no longer probes that endpoint — it just uses `kimi-for-coding`.
- **No `response_format`** → set Kimi's `supportsJSONResponseFormat = false`; the coding endpoint rejects that field (a known 401 trigger). JSON tasks now request JSON via the prompt + tolerant parsing instead.

Net: with a valid key from the **Kimi Code Console** and base URL `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`, it should now authenticate and run.

### 2. Per-provider API keys
The keys were already stored per-provider in the Keychain (`apikey.<provider>`), but switching providers could leave the editor showing the previous provider's value because SwiftUI reused the same field. I added `.id(provider)` to the API-key field (and the Base URL field) so each provider gets a fresh editor bound to its own stored key. Updated the footer to say keys are stored "separately for each provider" (localized).

### 3. Base URL layout
The Base URL used a `LabeledContent` with a 240pt right-aligned field, so a URL like `api.kimi.com/coding/v1` wrapped onto two lines with empty space beside it. I moved the label above a full-width single-line field — it now renders on one line.

Localization: the one changed user-facing string got its `zh-Hans` translation updated in place (no key reordering); `Base URL` already existed.

One thing to confirm on your end: make sure the key you pasted came from **kimi.com/code/console** (the Code console), not platform.kimi.ai — the "Get an API key" link in the app now takes you to the right place.

Both platforms build clean (`** BUILD SUCCEEDED **`, zero warnings), `in Sources == 0`, pbxproj clean.

## Both iOS UI issues fixed

### 1. Photo Translate buttons (screenshot 2 — the badly broken one)
The Camera Scan / Photos / Files buttons used icon-beside-text labels at `.controlSize(.large)`. Three of them shared a narrow iPhone row, so the prominent button's padding squeezed "Camera Scan" below word-width and it wrapped **letter-by-letter into a tall circle**.

I replaced them with a shared `sourceButtonLabel` that stacks **icon over text** vertically, giving the title the button's full width with `.fitSingleLine(0.6)`. Now each button is a clean equal-width tile with the label on one line — no wrapping. (Dropped the redundant `.controlSize(.large)`; the label's own padding sets the height.)

### 2. "More → More" tab redundancy (screenshot 1)
The app declared **8 tabs**, so iOS collapsed the overflow (Learn, Phrases, Stats, **More**) into an auto-generated system "More" list — with the app's own More hub nested inside it.

I consolidated iOS to **5 tabs** (Translate, Photo, History, Vocabulary, More) so there's no system overflow. Learn / Phrases / Stats now live inside the More hub under a new **"Learning Tools"** section (`NavigationLink`s pushing onto the hub's own stack). Applied to both the modern (`.sidebarAdaptable`) and iOS-17 legacy `TabView`.

To keep the **Siri "start review" deep-link** working: `AppRouteStore.triggerReview` now targets the More tab on iOS, and `MoreView` watches for that pending action and pushes the Learn screen automatically — so `LearnView` still consumes the action exactly as before. macOS is unaffected (it shows these as sidebar items and still routes to `.learn` directly), and I verified the macOS build.

Localization: "Learning Tools" added with `zh-Hans` = 学习工具. I deliberately avoided reusing the existing "Learning" key, which is translated as 学习中 ("in progress") — wrong for a section header.

A note on scope: this tab consolidation is the IA change the prior handoff had flagged as deferred/risky. I kept it behavior-preserving and build-verified on both platforms, but since I can't run the simulator here, it's worth a quick manual check of two flows: (a) tapping More → Learn/Phrases/Stats navigates correctly, and (b) a Siri "start review" shortcut lands on the Learn screen.
